topic: Rib pain after coughing or twisting

slides.headline: Sharp rib pain after a big cough?
slides.sub: Why ribs get sore, and how to stay comfortable while they settle.

slides.title: Ribs move with every breath
slides.body: Your ribs connect to your spine and breastbone through small joints and muscles between each rib. A hard cough, sneeze or awkward twist can strain them, and they often complain for a while.

slides.title: Why it catches on a deep breath
slides.body: Coughing, laughing and rolling over in bed all move the ribs. That's why pain can feel sharp on these movements yet ease when you're still. It's usually irritation, not harm.

slides.title: Keep breathing deeply
slides.body: Shallow breathing to avoid pain can leave you stiffer. A few slow, deep breaths each hour, and hugging a pillow when you cough, can make things more comfortable.

slides.title: Gentle movement helps
slides.body: Easy walking, slow side bends and gentle rotation within comfort usually help more than staying rigid. Many rib strains settle over a few weeks as you keep moving.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: See your GP promptly for chest pain with breathlessness, fever, coughing up blood, pain after a fall or knock, or pain that is severe or getting worse. Call 000 in an emergency.

caption:
Sharp pain in your ribs every time you cough, sneeze or roll over?

Summer colds and a hard cough, or a quick twist reaching for something, can strain the small joints and muscles around the ribs. Pain on a deep breath or when you roll in bed is common, and most people find it settles over a few weeks.

What tends to help: slow deep breaths through the day, hugging a pillow when you cough, and gentle walking and rotation instead of staying rigid. Chest pain with breathlessness, fever or pain after a fall needs your GP first.

story.headline: Ribs hurt when you cough?
story.body: Hug a pillow to your chest when you cough, and take five slow, deep breaths every hour.
